purpose: machine-readable ontology of the end-to-end applied data-analysis pipeline as evaluable work units, from estimand framing through cleaning, missing-data handling, modeling, diagnostics, uncertainty reporting, and reproducible, non-deceptive release, as a subdomain node of quantitative/statistical analysis and causal inference for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Data Analysis Workflow is modeled as a subdomain of quantitative/statistical analysis and causal inference.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable pipeline stages or analysis decisions, not topics.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows Wickham & Grolemund (2017), Tukey (1977), Gelman & Hill (2006), and Little & Rubin (2019) framing of EDA, modeling, missing data, and reproducible/honest analysis.
exclusions: Study design and sampling decisions made before data exist (covered by research_design).
Deep causal-identification theory and instrument design beyond mapping estimands to admissible models.
Data engineering infrastructure, storage, and large-scale pipeline operations.

competency_questions.question: Given the substantive question, what is the target estimand, unit, and population the analysis must produce?
What does exploratory analysis reveal about distributions and relationships before modeling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EDA nodes produce distribution and relationship summaries

competency_questions.question: How does EDA motivate transform and feature decisions without becoming result-driven?
How is raw data turned into a tidy, validated analysis table and how is integrity asserted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DATA_CLEANING and DATA_VALIDATION present and ordered

competency_questions.question: How are outliers and anomalies detected and handled without result-driven deletion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OUTLIER_HANDLING with pre-specified rule and sensitivity

competency_questions.question: Which missing-data mechanism applies and which handling method is therefore valid?
Which feature transforms and encodings are chosen and how is leakage avoided?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FEATURE_TRANSFORM specifies transforms with a leakage check

competency_questions.question: How is the model family selected to match the outcome type and dependence, and parameters estimated?
Which diagnostics check model assumptions, collinearity, and influence?
How is uncertainty quantified and reported, and the result mapped back to the estimand?
How robust are conclusions to alternative specifications and untestable assumptions?
How does the workflow prevent p-hacking and the garden of forking paths?
How is the analysis made reproducible from raw data to result?
What independent review and replication gate releasing the results, and what limits claims?

glossary.definition: the target quantity the analysis aims to estimate
a table with one observation per row and one variable per column
missing completely at random; missingness independent of all data
missing at random; missingness depends only on observed data
missing not at random; missingness depends on unobserved values
creating several completed datasets and pooling estimates via Rubin's rules
using information unavailable at prediction time in a feature or split
regression with a link function for non-normal outcomes
the degree to which single observations change a fitted coefficient
high correlation among predictors that inflates coefficient variance
analysis-contingent decisions that invalidate naive p-values
quantifying how conclusions change under alternative assumptions
interleaving executable code, output, and narrative in one document
obtaining identical results by rerunning the same pipeline on the same data

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from applied data-analysis and reproducibility literature (e.g., Wickham & Grolemund 2017; Tukey 1977; Gelman & Hill 2006; Little & Rubin 2019) and standard practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Translate the substantive question and target estimand into an explicit analysis plan, units, population, and the decision the analysis must inform before touching data.
contradictors: model-first analyst who fits before framing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the target estimand shifts between descriptive, predictive, and causal

pros.claim: anchors every downstream wrangling, modeling, and reporting choice to a real estimand
pros.example: deciding the target is a causal average treatment effect vs a predictive score changes the entire pipeline

cons.claim: a vague or shifting question invalidates model and reporting decisions
cons.example: fitting a regression without a defined estimand yields coefficients no one can interpret as an answer

failure_modes: unit of analysis mismatched to the claim
acceptance_tests: estimand, population, and unit are written before data work
decision the analysis supports is stated
revisit_triggers: question reframed from descriptive to causal

nodes.definition: Inspect univariate and bivariate distributions, ranges, central tendency, spread, and skew to learn the data's shape before modeling.
contradictors: confirmatory-only analyst who skips EDA

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a variable's distribution differs markedly from the modeling assumption

pros.claim: surfaces shape, scale, and surprises that dictate transforms and model family
pros.example: a heavy right skew in income flags a log transform before linear modeling

cons.claim: informal looking encourages overfitting the eye and unprincipled choices
cons.example: spotting a 'pattern' in noise leads to a transform that does not replicate

failure_modes: EDA used to silently pick hypotheses (forking paths)
acceptance_tests: each modeled variable has an inspected distribution

nodes.definition: Build graphical displays (scatter, boxplots, faceting, conditioning plots) to reveal structure, relationships, and anomalies that summaries hide.
contradictors: table-only analyst who distrusts plots

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a plot contradicts the assumed functional form

pros.claim: plots reveal nonlinearity, interaction, and clustering that statistics summarize away
pros.example: a scatter shows a U-shaped relationship a correlation reports as ~0

cons.claim: visual pattern-hunting invites confirmation bias and selective emphasis
cons.example: cherry-picking the one facet that looks significant

acceptance_tests: each key relationship has at least one diagnostic plot

nodes.definition: Reshape, type-cast, join, deduplicate, and standardize raw data into a tidy analysis-ready table with documented transformations.
contradictors: analyst who models on raw untidy data

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when cleaning rules change the analytic sample size or composition

pros.claim: a tidy, documented table makes every later step reproducible and auditable
pros.example: one row per unit-period lets the same model script run after any data refresh

cons.claim: silent or undocumented cleaning quietly changes results and blocks reproduction
cons.example: an undocumented join that drops 8% of rows biases the sample

acceptance_tests: row counts before/after each join are logged
every transform is scripted, not manual

nodes.definition: Run schema, range, uniqueness, and consistency checks that assert the cleaned data meets documented expectations before analysis proceeds.
contradictors: analyst who trusts data without assertions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a validation check fails or expectations change

pros.claim: automated assertions catch corruption before it propagates into estimates
pros.example: a range check flags impossible negative ages introduced by a bad merge

cons.claim: over-strict rules reject valid edge values; too-loose rules pass corruption
cons.example: rejecting legitimately high outliers as 'invalid' silently truncates the distribution

failure_modes: validation skipped after a data refresh
checks too permissive to catch corruption
acceptance_tests: schema/range/uniqueness checks run and pass or are explicitly waived

nodes.definition: Detect, diagnose, and decide a principled, pre-registered treatment for outliers and influential anomalies without silently deleting inconvenient data.
contradictors: analyst who deletes points to improve fit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the outlier treatment changes the sign or significance of a key estimate

pros.claim: a pre-specified rule prevents result-driven deletion and keeps inference honest
pros.example: deciding to winsorize at the 1st/99th percentile before fitting, not after seeing p-values

cons.claim: ad hoc deletion is a major researcher-degrees-of-freedom and p-hacking channel
cons.example: dropping the three points that make the effect non-significant

failure_modes: treating data-entry errors and true extremes identically
acceptance_tests: handling rule fixed before seeing model results
results reported with and without outlier handling

nodes.definition: Characterize the missingness mechanism (MCAR/MAR/MNAR) and pattern to determine which handling methods are valid for the estimand.
contradictors: analyst who deletes incomplete rows by default
inputs: domain knowledge of why data are missing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when missingness is plausibly outcome-dependent (MNAR)

pros.claim: the mechanism decides whether listwise deletion, MI, or a selection model is even valid
pros.example: MAR justifies multiple imputation; MNAR demands an explicit selection/pattern-mixture model

cons.claim: mechanism is untestable from data alone and wrong assumptions bias estimates
cons.example: assuming MAR when dropout is outcome-driven biases the treatment effect

acceptance_tests: mechanism assumption is stated and justified with auxiliary evidence
sensitivity to mechanism assumption is reported

nodes.definition: Apply a mechanism-appropriate handling method (multiple imputation, full-information likelihood, or principled deletion) and propagate imputation uncertainty.
contradictors: analyst who mean-imputes and ignores added uncertainty

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when single imputation is used in place of multiple imputation

pros.claim: proper MI restores efficiency and yields standard errors that reflect missingness
pros.example: pooling 20 imputations gives wider, honest CIs versus single-imputation overconfidence

cons.claim: single/mean imputation understates uncertainty and biases associations
cons.example: mean imputation shrinks variance and inflates apparent precision

failure_modes: single imputation treated as complete data
imputation model omits the outcome or auxiliaries
acceptance_tests: imputation uncertainty is pooled via Rubin's rules
imputation model is congenial with the analysis model
revisit_triggers: analysis model changes the variables used

nodes.definition: Decide pre-specified variable transformations, encodings, scaling, and derived features that respect the estimand and avoid leakage.
contradictors: analyst who searches transforms to maximize fit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a transform is selected based on its effect on the p-value

pros.claim: principled transforms linearize relationships and stabilize variance for valid modeling
pros.example: log-transforming a skewed cost outcome makes additive effects interpretable

cons.claim: transform-hunting on the outcome is a forking-paths and leakage risk
cons.example: selecting the encoding that maximizes R-squared on the full data leaks test information

failure_modes: target leakage from future or outcome-derived features
transform chosen post hoc to improve significance
acceptance_tests: transforms are pre-specified or justified by EDA, not by model output
no feature uses information unavailable at prediction time

nodes.definition: Choose the model family and link function (OLS, GLM, multilevel) whose structure matches the outcome type, dependence, and estimand.
contradictors: analyst who defaults to OLS for every outcome

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the outcome type or dependence structure differs from the model's assumptions

pros.claim: matching family to outcome and dependence structure is prerequisite to valid inference
pros.example: logistic GLM for a binary outcome instead of a linear-probability model with out-of-range fits

cons.claim: a misspecified family produces biased, mis-calibrated estimates regardless of fit
cons.example: OLS on count data yields negative predictions and wrong standard errors

failure_modes: ignoring clustering/dependence (treating multilevel data as independent)
link function mismatched to outcome support
acceptance_tests: family matches outcome type and dependence structure
specification rationale is documented

nodes.definition: Estimate the chosen model's parameters and obtain point estimates, standard errors, and the fitted object for the target estimand.
contradictors: analyst who reports coefficients without an adjustment rationale

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when variable selection becomes outcome-driven rather than pre-specified

pros.claim: produces the estimate the question needs, with an explicit adjustment set
pros.example: adjusting for confounders chosen from a DAG, not from stepwise p-values

cons.claim: data-driven variable selection invalidates the reported standard errors
cons.example: stepwise selection produces optimistic SEs and unstable coefficients

failure_modes: adjustment set chosen by significance rather than by confounding logic
acceptance_tests: adjustment set is justified before fitting
estimate maps to the pre-stated estimand

nodes.definition: Check residual behavior, linearity, homoscedasticity, normality where relevant, and overall fit against the model's stated assumptions.
contradictors: analyst who reports estimates without checking residuals

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a diagnostic reveals a violation that changes the estimate's validity

pros.claim: diagnostics expose assumption violations that bias estimates or standard errors
pros.example: a funnel-shaped residual plot reveals heteroscedasticity needing robust SEs

cons.claim: passing-looking diagnostics can mask subtle misspecification
cons.example: residuals look fine but an omitted interaction biases a subgroup estimate

acceptance_tests: residual diagnostics run for every reported model
detected violations are addressed or disclosed

nodes.definition: Assess multicollinearity and influential/high-leverage observations that destabilize coefficients and distort the estimate.
contradictors: analyst who ignores leverage and reports unstable coefficients

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an influential subset materially changes a reported coefficient

pros.claim: detects when a few points or correlated predictors drive the result
pros.example: a single high-leverage hospital flips the sign of a treatment coefficient

cons.claim: mechanically dropping influential points can itself bias inference
cons.example: removing leverage points to stabilize a coefficient hides real heterogeneity

failure_modes: influential points silently driving the estimate
acceptance_tests: influence and collinearity are assessed for reported models
coefficient stability under point deletion is checked

nodes.definition: Report estimates with honest uncertainty (confidence/credible intervals, correct standard errors) rather than point estimates or bare p-values.
contradictors: analyst who reports only point estimates or stars

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reported standard errors do not account for clustering or multiplicity

pros.claim: intervals communicate precision and prevent over-reading a single estimate
pros.example: a wide CI crossing zero tempers a 'significant' headline effect

cons.claim: naive intervals understate uncertainty when SEs or multiplicity are wrong
cons.example: uncorrected CIs across 40 outcomes guarantee spurious 'findings'

failure_modes: reporting p-values without effect sizes or intervals
acceptance_tests: every reported estimate carries an interval
standard errors match the dependence structure

nodes.definition: Validate predictive/inferential stability via held-out checks, cross-validation, or sensitivity analyses across reasonable specifications.
contradictors: analyst who reports a single in-sample model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when results are not stable across reasonable alternative specifications

pros.claim: robustness across specifications guards against fragile, specification-dependent claims
pros.example: a specification curve shows the effect holds across 90% of defensible models

cons.claim: cross-validation on leaked or dependent data overstates performance
cons.example: random CV folds on time-series data leak future into past

failure_modes: single specification reported as if unique
acceptance_tests: result stability is checked across reasonable specifications
validation respects data dependence structure

nodes.definition: Interleave code, output, and narrative in an executable document so results regenerate from data and reasoning is traceable.
contradictors: analyst who copies numbers into a separate report

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a reported number can no longer be regenerated from the source

pros.claim: every reported number is regenerable from code, eliminating copy-paste error
pros.example: a Quarto doc rebuilds all tables from the dataset on a single render

cons.claim: monolithic notebooks can hide hidden state and out-of-order execution
cons.example: running cells out of order produces a report that does not reproduce on a clean run

failure_modes: manually pasted numbers diverging from code
acceptance_tests: report regenerates from data in a clean run
reported numbers trace to code

nodes.definition: Capture the analysis as an ordered, re-runnable pipeline with pinned dependencies and seeds so the full result reproduces from raw inputs.
contradictors: analyst who runs steps manually in an undocumented order

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when re-running the pipeline does not reproduce the reported result

pros.claim: pinned env plus ordered pipeline makes results reproduce on another machine
pros.example: a lockfile and seed let a reviewer rerun the whole analysis and get identical numbers

cons.claim: heavy tooling adds maintenance cost that small analyses may not need
cons.example: containerizing a one-off exploratory script can outweigh its benefit

acceptance_tests: pipeline reruns from raw data to result
dependencies and seeds are pinned

nodes.definition: Pre-register or transparently distinguish confirmatory from exploratory analysis and disclose all decisions to avoid p-hacking and forking-paths bias.
contradictors: analyst who tries many models and reports the best

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an analytic choice is made or reported conditional on the result it produces

pros.claim: separating confirmatory from exploratory keeps p-values and claims interpretable
pros.example: labeling a subgroup finding 'exploratory' prevents overclaiming a chance result

cons.claim: undisclosed flexibility manufactures false positives that do not replicate
cons.example: trying five outcome codings and reporting the one with p<0.05

failure_modes: post hoc hypotheses presented as a priori (HARKing)
acceptance_tests: confirmatory analyses are pre-specified before seeing outcomes
all analytic decisions and dead ends are disclosed

nodes.definition: Quantify how conclusions change under plausible alternative assumptions about missingness, outliers, confounding, and specification.
contradictors: analyst who reports one estimate as definitive

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the conclusion reverses under a plausible alternative assumption

pros.claim: shows whether conclusions survive defensible changes to untestable assumptions
pros.example: an E-value shows how strong unmeasured confounding must be to nullify the effect

cons.claim: sensitivity ranges can be gamed by choosing implausibly narrow alternatives
cons.example: only perturbing assumptions that leave the result intact

failure_modes: sensitivity bounds chosen to flatter the result
acceptance_tests: key untestable assumptions are stress-tested
conclusion's dependence on assumptions is reported

nodes.definition: Map model output back to the estimand and substantive claim, bounding what the design and data license and what they do not.
contradictors: analyst who reads causation into association

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the substantive claim exceeds what the design and estimand license

pros.claim: binds claims to what the estimand and design actually support
pros.example: stating an association, not a cause, when the design is observational

cons.claim: over-generalization and causal overreach are the most common reporting failures
cons.example: a single-site result reported as a universal effect

acceptance_tests: claim scope matches design and estimand
limitations on causality and generalization are stated

nodes.definition: Have an independent analyst rerun the pipeline and review decisions end-to-end before results are finalized or released.
contradictors: team that ships analyses without a second pair of eyes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when results are released without an independent reproduction

pros.claim: an independent rerun catches non-reproducibility and undisclosed decisions before release
pros.example: a reviewer's clean-environment rerun reveals a number that does not reproduce

cons.claim: review gating adds latency and can become a rubber stamp if rushed
cons.example: a hurried sign-off that skips the actual rerun gives false assurance

failure_modes: sign-off without an actual independent rerun
acceptance_tests: an independent analyst reproduces the headline results
decision log is reviewed before release
revisit_triggers: pipeline or report changes after review

edges.why_related: cleaning targets are defined by the estimand and unit framed first
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tidy table is shaped to the analysis the question needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: cleaning before framing reshapes data wrongly
edges.example: framing 'one row per patient-visit' tells cleaning how to aggregate
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates; recut data if the estimand changes

edges.why_related: the estimand determines which model family can answer it
edges.benefit_of_coupling: model structure is chosen to estimate the stated quantity
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking a model before the estimand yields the wrong target
edges.example: a causal estimand forces an adjustment/identification strategy, not a predictive model
edges.resolution_rule: estimand dominates model convenience

edges.why_related: the confirmatory/exploratory split is defined by the pre-stated plan
edges.benefit_of_coupling: pre-specification makes later p-values interpretable
edges.risk_of_conflict: without a plan there is no confirmatory baseline
edges.example: the analysis plan fixes the primary hypothesis before data are seen
edges.resolution_rule: plan-defined confirmatory set dominates post hoc additions

edges.why_related: validation asserts expectations on the cleaned table
edges.benefit_of_coupling: corruption is caught before analysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: validating raw data misses cleaning-induced errors
edges.example: range checks run on the tidy table after type coercion
edges.resolution_rule: validation gates the cleaned artifact

edges.why_related: mechanism diagnosis needs a validated missingness map
edges.benefit_of_coupling: mechanism reasoning rests on trustworthy missingness counts
edges.risk_of_conflict: diagnosing on corrupt data misreads the mechanism
edges.example: validated nullity flags feed the MCAR/MAR/MNAR assessment
edges.resolution_rule: validated data gates mechanism work

edges.why_related: the handling method must match the diagnosed mechanism
edges.benefit_of_coupling: valid imputation/deletion follows from the mechanism
edges.risk_of_conflict: handling before diagnosis risks an invalid method
edges.example: MAR justifies MI; MNAR needs a selection model
edges.resolution_rule: mechanism dictates the admissible handling set

edges.why_related: outlier decisions require validated, type-correct values
edges.benefit_of_coupling: true extremes are separated from data errors
edges.risk_of_conflict: handling outliers on unvalidated data conflates errors and extremes
edges.example: a flagged impossible value is a data error, not an outlier to winsorize
edges.resolution_rule: validation precedes outlier treatment

edges.why_related: distribution inspection surfaces the anomalies to be handled
edges.benefit_of_coupling: handling targets the anomalies EDA reveals
edges.risk_of_conflict: handling without EDA misses or mistreats anomalies
edges.example: a long tail seen in a histogram drives the winsorization decision
edges.resolution_rule: EDA-identified anomalies feed the handling rule

edges.why_related: transform choices follow from observed distribution shape
edges.benefit_of_coupling: transforms are motivated by data shape, not by fit
edges.risk_of_conflict: transforming before EDA is unmotivated
edges.example: observed skew motivates a log transform
edges.resolution_rule: EDA-justified transforms are preferred over fit-driven ones

edges.why_related: plots reveal nonlinearity that informs derived features
edges.benefit_of_coupling: feature form matches visualized relationships
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping plots hides needed nonlinear terms
edges.example: a curved scatter motivates a spline or quadratic term
edges.resolution_rule: visual evidence guides feature form

edges.why_related: the feature/encoding set shapes the candidate model family
edges.benefit_of_coupling: model family fits the prepared design matrix
edges.risk_of_conflict: selecting a model before features mismatches inputs
edges.example: categorical encodings determine whether a GLM or GAM is appropriate
edges.resolution_rule: features are fixed before family choice

edges.why_related: fitting requires a chosen family and link
edges.benefit_of_coupling: estimation runs on a justified specification
edges.risk_of_conflict: fitting before selection risks the wrong family
edges.example: logistic fit follows a binary-outcome family choice
edges.resolution_rule: selection gates estimation

edges.why_related: diagnostics operate on a fitted model's residuals
edges.benefit_of_coupling: assumption checks validate the fit
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting before diagnostics hides violations
edges.example: residual-vs-fitted plots come from the fitted object
edges.resolution_rule: fit precedes diagnostics; diagnostics can force refit

edges.why_related: influence and VIF are computed from the fitted design
edges.benefit_of_coupling: coefficient stability is assessed post-fit
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring influence leaves unstable estimates unflagged
edges.example: Cook's distance is computed from the fitted model
edges.resolution_rule: fit precedes influence analysis

edges.why_related: diagnostic outcomes determine which standard errors are valid
edges.benefit_of_coupling: reported intervals use diagnostics-appropriate SEs
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting before diagnostics yields wrong SEs
edges.example: detected heteroscedasticity switches reporting to robust SEs
edges.resolution_rule: diagnostics gate the SE choice

edges.why_related: intervals are built from the fitted estimates and SEs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: uncertainty is reported around the actual estimate
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting without the fit has nothing to bound
edges.example: a CI is formed from the coefficient and its SE
edges.resolution_rule: fit supplies the estimate the interval surrounds

edges.why_related: imputation pooling changes the reported standard errors
edges.benefit_of_coupling: intervals reflect missing-data uncertainty
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring imputation variance understates uncertainty
edges.example: Rubin's-rules pooling widens the reported CI
edges.resolution_rule: pooled SEs dominate complete-case SEs when data are imputed

edges.why_related: validation tests the fitted model out of sample or across specs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: robustness is assessed for the fitted model
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming results without validation overstates stability
edges.example: cross-validation evaluates the fitted predictive model
edges.resolution_rule: fit precedes validation

edges.why_related: sensitivity perturbs assumptions behind the reported estimate
edges.benefit_of_coupling: robustness of the interval to assumptions is quantified
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting without sensitivity hides assumption-dependence
edges.example: an E-value contextualizes the reported effect's fragility
edges.resolution_rule: sensitivity extends, not replaces, the primary interval

edges.why_related: interpretation maps reported intervals back to the claim
edges.benefit_of_coupling: claims are bounded by reported uncertainty
edges.risk_of_conflict: interpreting point estimates overstates certainty
edges.example: a CI crossing zero tempers the substantive claim
edges.resolution_rule: reported uncertainty bounds the interpretation

edges.why_related: sensitivity results change how strongly conclusions can be stated
edges.benefit_of_coupling: interpretation reflects assumption-robustness
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring sensitivity overstates conclusions
edges.example: a result that flips under plausible MNAR is interpreted cautiously
edges.resolution_rule: sensitivity tempers the strength of the claim

edges.why_related: the pipeline encodes the cleaning steps as re-runnable code
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cleaning is reproducible from raw data
edges.risk_of_conflict: manual cleaning breaks reproduction
edges.example: the cleaning script is a pinned pipeline stage
edges.resolution_rule: scripted cleaning is required before pipeline capture

edges.why_related: the executable report regenerates the reported numbers
edges.benefit_of_coupling: every reported figure traces to code
edges.risk_of_conflict: pasting numbers breaks the code-to-claim link
edges.example: a Quarto doc renders the CI table from the model object
edges.resolution_rule: report content derives from computed results

edges.why_related: independent replication reruns the captured pipeline
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a reviewer reproduces results from raw inputs
edges.risk_of_conflict: review without a runnable pipeline cannot replicate
edges.example: the reviewer runs the pinned pipeline in a clean container
edges.resolution_rule: a runnable pipeline gates replication review

edges.why_related: the executable report is the artifact under review
edges.benefit_of_coupling: decisions and numbers are reviewable in one document
edges.risk_of_conflict: review of scattered outputs misses linkage
edges.example: the reviewer reads code, output, and narrative together
edges.resolution_rule: the literate report feeds the review

edges.why_related: review checks the disclosed decision log for forking-paths issues
edges.benefit_of_coupling: undisclosed flexibility is caught before release
edges.risk_of_conflict: review without the decision log misses p-hacking
edges.example: the reviewer audits whether the primary hypothesis was pre-specified
edges.resolution_rule: disclosure gates integrity review

edges.why_related: review verifies claims do not exceed what the design licenses
edges.benefit_of_coupling: overreach is caught before release
edges.risk_of_conflict: unreviewed interpretation risks public overclaiming
edges.example: the reviewer rejects causal language on an observational result
edges.resolution_rule: interpretation is reviewed before sign-off

edges.why_related: flexible outlier handling competes with pre-specified honesty
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances data quality against degrees-of-freedom control
edges.risk_of_conflict: result-driven deletion masquerades as cleaning
edges.example: winsorizing only when it helps the p-value is p-hacking
edges.resolution_rule: pre-specify the handling rule; report with and without it

edges.why_related: searching many specifications conflicts with confirmatory discipline
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances robustness search against multiplicity
edges.risk_of_conflict: specification search becomes selective reporting
edges.example: running a specification curve then reporting only the favorable region
edges.resolution_rule: pre-register the specification set or report the full curve

edges.why_related: transform/encoding flexibility competes with pre-specification
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances modeling flexibility against forking paths
edges.risk_of_conflict: transform-hunting inflates false positives
edges.example: trying five outcome codings and reporting the significant one
edges.resolution_rule: fix transforms a priori or disclose all tried

edges.why_related: richer models tempt overreaching interpretation beyond design support
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances model expressiveness against claim discipline
edges.risk_of_conflict: a fancy model is read as proving causation
edges.example: a multilevel model on observational data interpreted causally
edges.resolution_rule: interpretation is bounded by identification, not model complexity

edges.why_related: honest full uncertainty competes with a clean readable narrative
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances completeness against communicability
edges.risk_of_conflict: hedging is dropped to make the report read cleanly
edges.example: omitting the multiplicity caveat because it complicates the story
edges.resolution_rule: keep the uncertainty caveat; simplify wording, not substance

edges.why_related: both are reproducibility artifacts with overlapping content
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shared environment metadata avoids duplication
edges.risk_of_conflict: duplicated, drifting environment notes in two places
edges.example: the lockfile referenced by the pipeline and the report should match
edges.resolution_rule: single source of truth for environment; report references it

edges.why_related: numeric and graphical EDA are complementary views of the same data
edges.benefit_of_coupling: combined they catch what either misses
edges.risk_of_conflict: redundant effort if treated as separate phases
edges.example: a histogram and a boxplot describe the same distribution
edges.resolution_rule: use both as one EDA step, not two sequential locks

edges.why_related: influence diagnostics can trigger revisiting the outlier decision
edges.benefit_of_coupling: influential points found post-fit inform pre-processing
edges.risk_of_conflict: an endless delete-refit loop chasing stability
edges.example: a high-leverage point flagged at diagnostics reopens the handling rule
edges.resolution_rule: revisit handling at most once per influential set; stop when the pre-specified rule is restored

edges.why_related: diagnostic violations can trigger reselecting the model family
edges.benefit_of_coupling: misspecification detected leads to a better family
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded respecification loops to chase fit
edges.example: nonlinearity in residuals sends you back to add a GAM term
edges.resolution_rule: respecify at most twice and pre-register the trigger; stop when assumptions hold or are disclosed

conflict_axes.trigger: a data-dependent choice could be made to improve the result
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: pre-specification dominates result-driven flexibility; otherwise label exploratory and disclose
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a choice changes the sign or significance of the primary estimate

conflict_axes.trigger: a specification improves fit but violates assumptions or the estimand
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: assumption validity and estimand fidelity dominate raw fit metrics
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a higher-fit model fails diagnostics or mis-targets the estimand

conflict_axes.trigger: incomplete rows could be dropped for simplicity
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: mechanism-appropriate handling dominates default deletion when missingness is MAR/MNAR
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: listwise deletion drops a large or non-random share of data

conflict_axes.trigger: a cleaner narrative omits uncertainty or multiplicity caveats
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: honest uncertainty dominates narrative cleanliness; simplify wording, not substance
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a caveat material to the decision is dropped from the report

conflict_axes.trigger: stakeholders want a causal claim the design cannot license
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: design-licensed scope dominates desired causal strength; report association unless identification holds
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a causal claim is requested from observational data without an identification strategy

conflict_axes.trigger: a deadline pressures skipping pipeline capture or review
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reproducibility and review dominate speed for released results; drafts may relax
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: results are released without a reproducible pipeline or independent rerun

conflict_axes.trigger: deleting extremes would tidy results but may bias inference
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: pre-specified handling plus reported sensitivity dominates convenience deletion
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: deletion changes a key conclusion or removes a non-trivial data share

conflict_axes.trigger: a complex model fits better but obscures the estimand
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: estimand interpretability dominates marginal fit gains unless prediction is the goal
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: model complexity prevents mapping output back to the substantive claim

edge_cases.trigger: a join or filter silently drops rows
edge_cases.failure_mode: biased analytic sample from undocumented row loss
edge_cases.detection_method: compare row counts before/after each transform against expected keys

edge_cases.trigger: single/mean imputation used as if data were complete
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether imputation variance is pooled via Rubin's rules

edge_cases.trigger: outliers deleted after seeing their effect on results
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the handling rule timestamp/log precedes model results

edge_cases.trigger: causal language applied to an observational association
edge_cases.detection_method: check that claim scope matches the identification strategy and design

edge_cases.trigger: a feature uses outcome or future information
edge_cases.detection_method: audit each feature's availability time vs the prediction point
verify CV folds respect temporal/cluster structure
rerun the pipeline in a clean environment and diff outputs

edge_cases.trigger: out-of-order notebook execution leaves hidden state
edge_cases.failure_mode: report does not reproduce on a clean run
edge_cases.detection_method: restart kernel and run top-to-bottom; compare outputs

edge_cases.trigger: many tests reported without multiplicity control
edge_cases.detection_method: count tested hypotheses and check for correction or disclosure
resolution: apply multiplicity adjustment or report family

edge_cases.trigger: model assumptions never checked before reporting
edge_cases.detection_method: require a diagnostic artifact per reported model

edge_cases.trigger: a numeric score is labeled observed without data
edge_cases.detection_method: scan metric/value labels for observed/experimentally_validated without source eligibility

workflow.objective: fix estimand, population, unit, and the confirmatory/exploratory split
acceptance_tests: estimand and unit stated before data work
primary hypothesis pre-specified
workflow.do_first_because: framing anchors every downstream choice and prevents forking paths

workflow.objective: produce a tidy, validated analysis table with a transform log
acceptance_tests: transforms scripted
validation checks run
workflow.do_first_because: validated data prevents corruption propagating into every later estimate

workflow.objective: characterize distributions and relationships to motivate transforms
acceptance_tests: distribution and at least one plot per key variable
workflow.do_first_because: EDA must inform transforms before modeling, but stay exploratory to avoid forking paths

workflow.objective: diagnose missingness and anomalies and apply pre-specified handling
acceptance_tests: handling rule fixed before model results
imputation uncertainty pooled
workflow.do_first_because: mechanism-appropriate handling must precede modeling and be fixed before seeing results

workflow.objective: specify transforms/features and select the matching model family
acceptance_tests: transforms pre-specified or EDA-justified
family rationale documented
workflow.do_first_because: specification must be fixed before fitting to avoid fit-driven choices

workflow.objective: estimate parameters for the stated estimand with a justified adjustment set
acceptance_tests: estimate maps to the estimand
workflow.do_first_because: a justified fit is prerequisite to diagnostics and reporting

workflow.objective: check assumptions, influence, and robustness of the fitted model
acceptance_tests: violations addressed or disclosed
results stable across specifications
workflow.do_first_because: assumption and robustness checks must precede inference to avoid invalid SEs

workflow.objective: report estimates with honest uncertainty and design-bounded interpretation
acceptance_tests: SEs match dependence structure
claims bounded by estimand and design
workflow.do_first_because: honest uncertainty and bounded claims must be set before producing the report

workflow.objective: capture the analysis as an executable report and a pinned, re-runnable pipeline
acceptance_tests: clean-run reproduction succeeds
numbers trace to code
workflow.do_first_because: reproducibility must be captured before independent review and release

workflow.objective: independently reproduce and review decisions before sign-off
acceptance_tests: reviewer reproduces results
no undisclosed forking paths
workflow.do_first_because: no release before an independent reproduction and integrity review pass

priority_rationale.notes: tidy data gates analysis and pipeline
executable report links code to claims

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk stage is rushed to meet a deadline
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates delivery speed for released results
dominance_rules.required_action: run diagnostics and review before release
dominance_rules.example: do not skip diagnostics to ship a dashboard on time

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value stage is tempting to start before prerequisites
dominance_rules.required_action: complete prerequisites before the dependent stage
dominance_rules.example: do not fit before the estimand and family are fixed

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks evidential support
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels and observed fields at 0.0 absent data
dominance_rules.example: report a heuristic prior, not a falsely observed value

dominance_rules.trigger: an analytic choice would improve the result
dominance_rules.required_action: fix the choice a priori or label it exploratory and disclose
dominance_rules.example: do not pick the transform that maximizes significance

dominance_rules.trigger: a model is ready to report but unchecked
dominance_rules.rule: assumption/influence checks dominate eagerness to report
dominance_rules.example: do not publish SEs before checking heteroscedasticity

dominance_rules.trigger: results are about to be released without a human rerun
dominance_rules.rule: independent human review dominates automated release
dominance_rules.required_action: require an independent reproduction and sign-off
dominance_rules.example: no auto-publish without a reviewer's clean-run rerun

dominance_rules.trigger: a causal claim exceeds what the design supports
dominance_rules.rule: design-licensed scope dominates desired causal strength
dominance_rules.required_action: report association unless an identification strategy holds
dominance_rules.example: call an observational association an association

dominance_rules.trigger: incomplete rows are about to be dropped by default
dominance_rules.rule: mechanism-appropriate handling dominates default listwise deletion
dominance_rules.required_action: diagnose mechanism and choose a valid method
dominance_rules.example: use MI under MAR rather than deleting incomplete cases

dominance_rules.trigger: tooling is skipped to deliver faster
dominance_rules.rule: reproducibility dominates output-volume convenience for released work
dominance_rules.required_action: capture a runnable pipeline and executable report
dominance_rules.example: pin the environment even when the analysis feels small

dominance_rules.trigger: a higher-fit model violates assumptions or the estimand
dominance_rules.example: reject an overfit transform that breaks residual assumptions

dominance_rules.trigger: an object is created without a traceable source or reference
dominance_rules.required_action: link every claim to code, data, and decision log
dominance_rules.example: every reported number must trace to a code chunk

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix estimand and plan before touching data
anti_rework_rules.rationale: reframing after data work invalidates downstream choices and p-values
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: modeling starts with no written estimand
anti_rework_rules.example: do not start cleaning before the unit of analysis is fixed

anti_rework_rules.rationale: analyzing corrupt data forces full rework after detection
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: EDA or modeling runs on unvalidated data
anti_rework_rules.example: do not model before range and key checks pass

anti_rework_rules.rationale: handling chosen before diagnosis may be invalid and need redoing
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: imputation runs with no mechanism statement
anti_rework_rules.example: do not impute before assessing MCAR/MAR/MNAR

anti_rework_rules.rationale: unmotivated transforms get reverted after EDA
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a transform is applied with no distribution inspected
anti_rework_rules.example: do not log-transform before viewing the distribution

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose the model family before fitting
anti_rework_rules.rationale: fitting the wrong family wastes estimation effort
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a fit exists with no documented family rationale
anti_rework_rules.example: do not run OLS on counts then redo as Poisson

anti_rework_rules.rationale: reporting before checking assumptions forces retraction
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: intervals reported with no diagnostic artifact
anti_rework_rules.example: do not publish a CI before checking residuals

anti_rework_rules.rule: pre-specify or disclose analytic choices before making them
anti_rework_rules.rationale: result-driven choices require redoing the analysis honestly
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a choice is made after seeing its effect on results
anti_rework_rules.example: do not finalize outlier rules after seeing p-values

anti_rework_rules.rule: capture a runnable pipeline before review
anti_rework_rules.rationale: review without a pipeline cannot reproduce and stalls
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: review requested with no runnable pipeline
anti_rework_rules.example: do not request replication of un-pinned manual steps

anti_rework_rules.rule: run sensitivity before finalizing strong claims
anti_rework_rules.rationale: claims that flip under assumptions must be walked back
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a strong claim is made with no assumption stress-test
anti_rework_rules.example: do not assert robustness without an E-value or MNAR check

anti_rework_rules.rationale: releasing unreviewed results risks public correction
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: results released with no sign-off record
anti_rework_rules.example: do not publish before a reviewer reproduces the headline numbers

iteration_protocol.trigger: a validation check or diagnostic fails
acceptance_tests: each failure is recorded with severity
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no failing checks remain above threshold

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk x detectability
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defects addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a locked or high-coupling stage
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents via edges and priority_order
acceptance_tests: all dependents of a changed stage are revalidated

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to repair owner
acceptance_tests: repair owner matches failure type
repaired stage passes its checks
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes with no new failures

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence changes a node's importance
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed from priors and evidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a locked stage must change after review
acceptance_tests: lock downgrade has a change-control record

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk or uncertainty crosses the human-review threshold
acceptance_tests: high-risk decisions reach a human reviewer

test_cases.input_summary: single descriptive analysis with no missing data
stakeholder asks for causal effect from observational data

version_increment_rules: increment on any change to a hard-locked released artifact
increment when the estimand or population changes
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade requires a change-control record and revalidation
high-coupling stage downgrade forces revalidation of all dependents
human_approval_required_for: outlier deletion that changes a conclusion
